newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up, prices erratic on ringgit.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up, prices erratic on ringgit.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market ended higher on Tuesday, but prices remained erratic due to concerns over the volatility of the ringgit, said traders.
They said shortcovering demand was reported for the SMR10 and SMR20 after weeks of bearish sentiment.
But buyers and sellers had difficulty agreeing on prices because of differing opinions on whether the ringgit would weaken further or rebound in the near-term, said the traders.
"I think the market has much potential to go higher this week," said one trader.
The benchmark RSS1 buyer for August was officially priced at 231 cents (90 U.S. cents) a kg, up 2.50 cents from Monday's close. The SMR20 buyer for August was up two cents to 234.50.
Traders quoted the SMR 20 at 240 cents, SMR CV at 296, SMR L at 280, SMR5 at 247, SMR10 at 242 and drum latex at 193.
The INRO's five-day average price strengthened at 182.27 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 14, compared to 182.07 on July 11. The daily indicator rose to 183.92 from 182.63 previously.
The INRO would have had to intervene in the market to buy rubber if its five-day price fell below 172 cents. But traders said such a scenario has been averted for the time being.
Malaysian-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
